summary: Backend/HTTP-only test of the Nginx cache-control fix on https://cinemaries.fr. Created pytest suite at /app/backend/tests/test_nginx_cache_headers.py (12 tests). ALL 12 TESTS PASSED. Verified: (A) all 6 HTML SPA routes return Cache-Control containing 'no-store' and 'must-revalidate' + Pragma: no-cache; (B) hashed Expo asset /_expo/static/js/web/entry-*.js returns Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable; (C) /api/uploads/*.jpg returns 200 with long-cache header; (D) non-regression: homepage 200 + contains 'CINÉMARIÉS', /api/videos/public 200, /api/guestbook/active 200; (E) non-regression admin: login via /api/auth/login with contact@cinemaries.fr / Reset2026! returns 200 + token, and GET /api/admin/stats with token returns 200. The Nginx fix is confirmed live in production and does not regress any API. One cosmetic observation only.

minor.issue: Response contains TWO Cache-Control headers: 'no-cache' (from upstream Node/Expo server) and 'no-store, no-cache, must-revalidate' (added by Nginx). Browsers merge them so the strict Nginx value wins and behavior is correct, but it's slightly messy. To clean up, add 'proxy_hide_header Cache-Control;' before the 'add_header Cache-Control ...' directive in the location / block of /etc/nginx/sites-enabled/cinemaries. Purely cosmetic — the fix is fully functional.

Expires header returns a future date (e.g. 'Fri, 11 Sep 2026 23:24:09 GMT') instead of the intended 'Expires: -1'. Likely the upstream server sets its own Expires and Nginx add_header appends rather than replaces. Non-blocking because Cache-Control no-store takes precedence per RFC 7234, but recommend adding 'proxy_hide_header Expires;' before the 'add_header Expires -1;' directive for consistency.

action_items: OPTIONAL cosmetic cleanup only: in /etc/nginx/sites-enabled/cinemaries, add 'proxy_hide_header Cache-Control;' and 'proxy_hide_header Expires;' before the corresponding 'add_header' directives in the location / block, so upstream headers don't duplicate Nginx's. Not required — current behavior is correct because Cache-Control no-store wins over any duplicate/expires header.
No other action required. The Nginx cache-control fix is verified working in production.
critical_code_review_comments: Fix scope is Nginx-only (no application code touched) — the change is safe and minimal.
The chosen strategy (no-store on HTML + immutable long-cache on hashed assets) is the industry-standard pattern for SPA deployments and is correct here.
Recommend keeping this test file in the regression suite — future deployments/Nginx reloads should keep these 12 tests green.

rca_of_issue: Original bug: Chrome aggressively cached the buggy old admin HTML (infinite spinner) because Nginx sent no Cache-Control on SPA HTML responses. Fix: /etc/nginx/sites-enabled/cinemaries now adds 'Cache-Control: no-store, no-cache, must-revalidate' + 'Pragma: no-cache' + 'Expires: -1' on location / (HTML/SPA), and 'Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable' on location /_expo/ (fingerprinted JS/CSS assets). Verified live via curl HEAD on all 6 HTML routes and on a real hashed JS asset. Nginx was reloaded with 'nginx -s reload' (zero downtime). No app-code regression: /api/videos/public, /api/guestbook/active, /api/auth/login, /api/admin/stats all still return 200.
